title: Quarterly Runway: Predictive Warm Pools, Quota Smoothing, and Autoscale Guardrails
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Objective: Define and deliver a Q2 roadmap that reduces burst latency by 25% and reduces excess reserved cost by 10% for Dedicated customers through predictive warm pools, quota smoothing, and explicit autoscale guardrails. This ticket is the umbrella PM artifact to coordinate cross-team deliverables (runtime, infra, console, billing) and to capture milestones, acceptance criteria, and rollout cadence.

Scope: (1) Predictive warm pool controller prototype + telemetry hook; (2) Quota smoothing policies to avoid noisy bursts from tenant misconfiguration; (3) Autoscale guardrails + runbook for fast-fail and fallback to hosted variants; (4) Console UX for pool sizing recommendations and commit hedging hints.

Out of scope: model-level kernel improvements, billing pricing changes (pricing pilots will be tracked in a separate PM ticket).
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end demonstrator: warm pool controller can maintain a 10% prewarmed buffer for a sample customer workload with 95th-percentile allocation time < 350ms
Quota smoothing: new smoothing policy reduces peak-to-baseline request spikes by >= 40% in synthetic workload tests
Guardrails: autoscale policies include explicit fallback chain (same-region variant -> cross-region variant -> hosted fallback) and a validated canary runbook
Console: recommendations surfaced in the Dedicated Pool sizing panel with confidence band and estimated monthly $ impact
Telemetry: dashboard showing warm-pool hit rate, allocation latency, and false-positive scale-ups with < 15% false alarm rate
milestones: 2026-02-15: Kickoff + stakeholder alignment (runtime, infra, console, billing)
2026-03-05: Warm-pool controller v0 prototype (ENG-70112) and API contract draft
2026-03-20: Quota smoothing policy design review and simulation results
2026-03-31: Guardrail runbook + failure-mode rehearsals in staging
2026-04-10: Console UX mock sign-off and telemetry dashboard wired to staging metrics
notes:
Trade-offs: Prefill vs overprovisioning — we will favor predictive prefill with a conservative confidence threshold to avoid long tail cold starts while limiting reserved capacity. Kernel-level optimization still necessary for long-term latency gains but will be handled by runtime team (ENG-7xxx). Pricing impact: trade-off between dedicated reservation utilization and customer cost that we'll quantify in the console recommendations step.

Open questions: (1) What signal set is cost-effective for prediction (recent arrival rate, token distribution, user-level session persistence)? (2) How do we parameterize smoothing policies per-customer vs global defaults?
